clause: (6) a FOREIGN tenant cannot read, list, write into, or unbind another organization's environment, and cannot resolve its derived secret name even knowing it verbatim
now_false: NOT THE MEASUREMENT, WHICH WAS TAKEN AND HELD — five paths were driven as a second tenant and all five refused. What is false is the SUBJECT it names. There is no organization: A.2 dropped organization_id from every table, and on `environments` and `environment_values` it added no project_id in its place, so from A.2 until 2026-08-05 those tables carried the installation policy and all five of those paths REACHED. The clause was true when published, false for the whole interval between, and true again since migration 000006 — but of a PROJECT, which is not the noun this sentence uses. A reader re-running it against the tree finds a test with a different name asserting a boundary between projects; a reader trusting the noun looks for an organization that has not existed since A.2.
evidence: The proof this case listed for the clause is gone from the tree: `grep -rn 'TestAForeignTenantCannotReachAnotherOrgsEnvironment' --include='*.go' --include='*.yaml' . | grep -v ./evidence/` -> no match (2026-08-05). Its replacement is apps/control-plane/internal/identity/environments_component_test.go:TestAForeignProjectCannotReachAnotherProjectsEnvironment, which drives the same five paths and additionally asserts that the refused WRITE landed no row and that the owner's own value survived the foreign delete attempt. The interval in which the clause was false is itself recorded in the tree: the middle version of that test was named TestEnvironmentsAreInstallationWide and asserted that every one of the five paths reached.

clause: FOURTH CEILING: an environment is ORG-scoped, matching secret_refs, so two projects in one organization see the same environments — a product fact, stated on the screen T4 builds
now_false: FALSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE, which is why it is recorded separately from the clause above rather than folded into it. An environment is not ORG-scoped, because there are no organizations. And two projects do NOT see the same environments: migration 000006 keys `environments` on project_id and `environment_values` on its parent's, and `environments_name_key` is now UNIQUE (project_id, name) rather than UNIQUE (name), so two projects may each hold a `production` and neither can read the other's. The ceiling was an honest product statement about a real boundary; what supersedes it is that the boundary moved DOWN a level rather than being removed. What survives of it: rows written before 000006 carry an empty project_id and stay readable to every scope — that residue is the only sense in which two projects still share an environment, and it is bounded to pre-existing rows.
evidence: storage/migrations/000006_project_scoped_secrets_and_environments.up.sql adds the column and rebuilds both constraints; tests/security/tenancy/tenancy_test.go:TestOnlyUsageLedgerStaysInstallationWide asserts that a scoped tenant now sees ZERO of another tenant's environments and environment_values while usage_ledger stays wide, and the same file's confinement canary counts environments and environment_values as project-confined again. Both are run by `TEST=tenancy scripts/test/security` -> 22 PASS (2026-08-05). The screen the ceiling refers to states a product fact that has changed; the screen is T4's and is not edited by this record.
